subject: CRAN, MSVC, long long, C++11, size_t,  and other headaches

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: CRAN, MSVC, long long, C++11, size_t,  and other headaches
parts:
Can we just drop MSVC support now that we have g++
working? Then we could presumably get rid of this
file.

Does MSVC use different sizes than g++?

Which compiler and bit size are we using on Jenkins?

What's required for CRAN?

If I just leave everything alone with "long long", what
are the consequences?

Does someone else understand Boost fixed-size types or
the built-in fixed size macros well enough to help me out?

What I need is the following constructors for agrad::var:

var()
explicit var(vari*);
var(double);

What I want is to have every arithmetic type use the
var(double) constructor, but there are conflicts with
unsigned long and vari*, despite var(vari*) being explicit.

Yes, I can get enable_if working on my Mac to pick out
arithmetic types, but I can't get it to work on Windows, so
tests fail on Jenkins.

Previously, we just used all of the following
constructors:

var()
explicit var(vari* vi)
var(float), var(double), var(long double)
var(bool), var(short), var(int), var(long), *** var(long long) ***
var(unsigned short), var(unsigned int), var(unsigned long), *** var(unsigned long long) ***

The built-in types don't run into overload conflicts with each
other, but as soon as you get into the typedefs like size_t, uint64_t,
etc., the shit hits the fan when trying to overload.

The problem is that "long long" missed the boat for C++, so is only
in C++11.

Does using long long run afoul of CRAN policy.

The memory models in play are these:

ILP32 LP64 LLP64
char 8 8 8
short 16 16 16
int 32 32 32
long 32 64 32
long long 64 64 64
size_t 32 64 64
pointer 32 64 64

ILP32: 32-bit Windows
LP64: 64-bit linux & mac
LLP64: 64-bit windows

I can't for the life of me figure out how to get the right set of
constructors to cover all inputs and not run into conflicts without
using long long. And it looks like we can't get 64-bit integers
on ILP32 wihtout long long.

We could just punt altogether on long support in autodiff.
I think that'd require some serious test rewriting, and would be
less than ideal for third parties, but I think it may come to that.
We don't need it for running Stan models.

- Bob

parts:

Only stanc needs to be compiled on CRAN.  Can we just make stanc CRAN compatible?

Not quite. The vignette compiles models and that is what triggered these warnings.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: CRAN, MSVC, long long, C++11, size_t,  and other headaches
parts:
On Saturday, February 28, 2015 at 11:49:31 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Can we just drop MSVC support now that we have g++
working?  Then we could presumably get rid of this
file.
Someone on stan-users gor MSVC to work with a more recent Boost, so I think dropping MSVC support would be a last resort.
Does MSVC use different sizes than g++?
Probably not for MSVC >= 2012, which is what works with Boost
Which compiler and bit size are we using on Jenkins?
Not MSVC
What's required for CRAN?

Not MSVC; see

http://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html

If I just leave everything alone with "long long", what
are the consequences?
Would have to compile rstan in C++11 mode and thus not have a Snow Leopard binary.

Does someone else understand Boost fixed-size types or
the built-in fixed size macros well enough to help me out?
No but maybe
Does using long long run afoul of CRAN policy.
Without compiling in C++11 mode, yes.

We could just punt altogether on long support in autodiff.
I think that'd require some serious test rewriting, and would be
less than ideal for third parties, but I think it may come to that.
We don't need it for running Stan models.

I could patch the files that use long long for the StanHeaders package. However, that would slightly undermine the API if someone wanted to use StanHeaders in C++ mode. At this time, I think C++11 for rstan is not quite the right choice because we haven't done enough testing with how all the other code gets compiled.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: CRAN, MSVC, long long, C++11, size_t,  and other headaches
parts: On Saturday, February 28, 2015 at 11:49:31 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:

Previously, we just used all of the following
constructors:

  var()
  explicit var(vari* vi)
  var(float), var(double), var(long double)
  var(bool), var(short), var(int), var(long), *** var(long long) ***
  var(unsigned short), var(unsigned int), var(unsigned long), *** var(unsigned long long) ***

The built-in types don't run into overload conflicts with each
other, but as soon as you get into the typedefs like size_t, uint64_t,
etc., the shit hits the fan when trying to overload.

The problem is that "long long" missed the boat for C++, so is only
in C++11.

Can you put the long long constructors inside an ifdef that tests for C++11?

Ben
